case_name: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru & Ors. v. State of Kerala
facts: Challenge to the 24th, 25th, and 29th Amendments which curtailed fundamental rights and expanded Parliament's amending power.
holding: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, but cannot alter its 'Basic Structure'.

case_name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
facts: Challenge to the Aadhaar scheme on the grounds that it violated the right to privacy.
holding: Right to Privacy is a fundamental right intrinsic to life and liberty under Article 21.

case_name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
facts: Challenge to the constitutionality of Section 377 of the IPC which criminalized consensual same-sex sexual acts.
holding: Section 377 IPC is unconstitutional insofar as it criminalizes consensual sexual conduct between adults of the same sex.

case_name: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
facts: A PIL was filed addressing custodial deaths and police violence.
holding: Established detailed guidelines to be followed by police during arrest and detention to prevent custodial torture.

case_name: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P.
facts: Refusal by police to register an FIR based on a complaint of a cognizable offence.
holding: Registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence.

case_name: Vishaka & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan
facts: PIL filed after the gang rape of a social worker, Bhanwari Devi, demanding workplace safety.
holding: Laid down the 'Vishaka Guidelines' to prevent and address sexual harassment of women at the workplace.

case_name: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
facts: Challenge to the practice of Triple Talaq (talaq-e-biddat) among Muslims.
holding: The practice of instant Triple Talaq is unconstitutional and void as it violates Article 14.

facts: Conflict in interpretations of the 2005 amendment granting coparcenary rights to daughters.
holding: Daughters have equal coparcenary rights in Hindu Undivided Family property irrespective of whether the father was alive at the time of the 2005 amendment.

case_name: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa
facts: Dispute over the definition of 'industry' under the Industrial Disputes Act.
holding: Provided a broad definition of 'industry' based on the triple test: systematic activity, cooperation between employer and employee, and production of goods/services.

case_name: Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India
facts: Constitutional challenge to various provisions of the IBC.
holding: Upheld the constitutional validity of the IBC in its entirety, emphasizing the economic revival objective of the Code.

case_name: Gayatri Balasamy v. ISG Novasoft Technologies Ltd.
facts: Dispute on whether a court under Section 34 can modify an arbitral award.
holding: Court cannot modify the arbitral award under Section 34, it can only set it aside.

case_name: Vodafone International Holdings BV v. Union of India
facts: Tax department sought to tax the offshore transfer of shares between non-residents resulting in indirect transfer of Indian assets.
holding: Offshore share transactions not taxable in India unless explicitly provided by law. Led to retrospective taxation amendment.

case_name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
facts: Impounding of passport without giving reasons or a hearing.
holding: Article 21 requires the procedure established by law to be fair, just, and reasonable. Interlinked Articles 14, 19, and 21 ('Golden Triangle').

case_name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
facts: Challenge to Section 66A of the IT Act criminalizing online speech.
holding: Struck down Section 66A of the IT Act as unconstitutional for violating freedom of speech and expression (Article 19(1)(a)).

case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak Case)
facts: Leakage of oleum gas from Shriram Foods and Fertilizer Industries in Delhi.
holding: Established the principle of 'Absolute Liability' for hazardous industries, deviating from the Rylands v. Fletcher rule of strict liability.

case_name: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) v. Union of India
facts: PIL seeking legal recognition of transgender persons.
holding: Recognized transgender individuals as the 'third gender' and affirmed their fundamental rights under the Constitution.
